title: Compact row drag hit-area inconsistency and kinetic scroll mismatch across Safari/Firefox mobile
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Compact density mode introduces multiple cross-browser regressions: table row drag hit areas become effectively smaller on iOS Safari when text-scaling tokens are reduced; inertial/kinetic scrolling behavior differs between Safari and Firefox mobile leading to repeated mis-drops when dragging rows; compact button touch targets on high-density devices fall below recommended minimums. This ticket triages reports, captures repros across devices, coordinates a design + engineering fix, and records verification steps for release regression tests.
acceptance_criteria: Repro steps documented for iOS Safari, iPadOS, Android Firefox WebView, and desktop Firefox
Hit-area for row-drag targets increased without visual regressions across token scales
Kinetic scroll and drag interaction stabilized: row drag cancels gracefully when momentum scroll starts
Compact mode tokens are not globally changed; changes are component-scoped or theme-safe
Automated visual regression tests added for table row hitbox at compact/comfortable densities
Cross-browser QA sign-off obtained and release notes updated
steps_to_reproduce: On iPhone 13 / iOS 16.6 / Safari: Open kanban-like table in compact density, attempt to drag a row while performing a quick upward scroll; observe repeated drop attempts and mis-targeting
On Pixel 6 / Android 13 / Firefox mobile: With compact density and 120% system text scaling, long-press row drag then perform kinetic swipe; row is dropped unexpectedly or pointer offset occurs
On iPad / Safari: In landscape, sticky table header sometimes overlaps chart legend when momentum scroll ends, causing legend taps to trigger row selection
Desktop Firefox with reduced window width: compact toolbar buttons render smaller hit areas and keyboard focus outlines appear clipped
observed_behavior: Row drag handle requires precise touch in compact mode on Safari; inertial scrolling cancels drag intermittently and causes row to reinsert incorrectly. Chart legend and sticky header layering occasionally blocks intended touch targets. Compact buttons have reduced tappable areas on some mobile densities.
expected_behavior: Drag hit areas should meet touch minimums (44px) regardless of density token scaling; initiating a drag should suppress inertial scrolling until drag end or clear cancel semantics; sticky headers and chart legends should not occlude interactive elements; compact buttons should preserve accessible touch targets and visible focus outlines.
notes: Initial suspect: token scale for spacing in compact mode reduced padding on draggable rows
Engineering suggested an overlay 'touch-zone' layer that increases effective hit-area without changing visual spacing
Tradeoff: overlay adds pointer handling logic; must ensure no impact on pointer-events for nested interactive controls (checkboxes, links)
Alternative considered: globally increase compact token padding, rejected due to visual density impact on many pages
Chart legend overlap likely separate sub-issue but reproduces in same flow; will be handled in this ticket to avoid dual regressions
qa_updates: 2026-03-01: Triage notes added by Asha; initial device matrix captured (iOS Safari, iPadOS Safari, Android Firefox, Desktop FF/Chrome).
2026-03-04: Assigned to Liam; engineering proposed prototype overlay to increase touch zone. ENG requested component-level token override instead of global token changes.
2026-03-07: Prototype implemented in feature branch; visual QA shows no perceptible layout shift but additional pointer-event edge cases discovered for nested controls.
2026-03-09: Updated prototype: transparent padding layer added with pointer-events forwarding; new regression tests added to Percy story.
2026-03-11: Cross-browser smoke tests: iOS Safari reproduces much less mis-drops; Firefox Android still has intermittent offset when system text scaling > 110%.
2026-03-12: Follow-up engineering task created to normalize pointer coordinates in drag library to account for device pixel ratio; target update planned before 2026-03-20 release candidate.
decision_log: Use component-scoped transparent touch overlay to increase effective hit area rather than changing compact tokens globally
Avoid relying solely on CSS touch-action; implement small guard in drag library to suppress momentum scroll on long-press drags on iOS Safari
Keep chart legend layering fix in this ticket to ensure no occlusion regressions during the same QA cycle
Add regression snapshots for compact/comfortable densities in visual test suite
review_feedback: Priya Singh (PM): Confirmed customer workflows impacted when users rapidly reorganize lists on mobile — requested ship-window before next customer demo.
Ethan Morales (Engineering): Noted potential perf implications of extra DOM layers; will audit layout thrash and prefer hardware-accelerated transforms where possible.
Marta Ruiz (Accessibility): Asked to ensure increased hit areas are announced correctly for screen readers and focus order remains predictable.
